subject: Mid-quarter exec checkpoint: scope shift proposal & security evidence needed for QBR
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmedata.com
Date: 2026-10-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-quarter exec checkpoint: scope shift proposal & security evidence needed for QBR

Team —

Quick mid-quarter check-in ahead of the QBR prep week. Two interlocking asks where I need quick alignment so we can lock the slides and the action grid by next Tuesday (10/21):

1) Rescope proposal (product):
- Proposal: reduce Q4 objective for "Optimize" delivery (latency & batching rollout) from "full roll to all Hosted customers" to "pilot to three marquee accounts + internal beta". This lowers initial launch scope and preserves reliability SLA targets.
- Rationale: current infra backlog + longer kernel validation window means full roll risks regressions.
- Expected impact: ~20% lower token-handling revenue in Q4 for Optimize feature; tradeoff buys 6 weeks of runway to harden telemetry.

2) Security/compliance evidence for Acme's procurement and our QBR:
- Acme procurement has asked for SOC 2 Type II attestation, data flow diagram showing telemetry retention, and confirmation on KMS/HSM options for private deployments.
- Requested: Laura, can you confirm what evidence we can include in the QBR appendix? Naomi, can you confirm if our internal artifact set (SOC doc, dataflow PNG, KMS design note) is cleared to share with Acme under current NDA?

Attachments: QBR-draft-v2.pdf (deck), MVP-scope-slide.pptx (proposed narrowed scope)

Timing: Please reply with your alignment + any redlines by EOD Monday 10/19. If we agree, I'll update the QBR deck and run a 30-minute prep on Wednesday (10/22) with execs.

Thanks —
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Product Strategy | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs: QBR-draft-v2.pdf (21 slides), MVP-scope-slide.pptx (1 slide)

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear ask. I'm +1 on the narrower pilot for Optimize for Q4. Two follow-ups:
- Can product commit to a single performance metric for the pilot (p99 latency target) so the story is crisp in the deck? If yes, put that number in the slide and we're good.
- Procurement timeline: Acme usually takes 3–4 weeks for PO processing once they have SOC 2 and a clear SLA. I'll ping Acme for an internal lead and ask them to confirm SLA expectations.

Naomi — please confirm the set of shareable artifacts we can attach to the QBR deck (SOC, dataflow, KMS note). If anything is redlined, call it out and we'll mark as "under review" in the appendix.

I'll hold off on the exec prep invite until we have the asset list.

Laura

Folks —

I support the rescope with the following conditions:
1) Product commits to the pilot p99 latency target (suggest 150ms for the three pilot accounts) and a clear rollback criterion.
2) Infrastructure needs clarity on additional capacity and staffing: to avoid queue backpressure we need 2w of dedicated infra effort plus 1 SRE contractor for kernel validation during the pilot. That's a cost we should factor into the QBR ask (rescope impact).
3) Procurement exception: if Acme requires prepaying credits or an SLA variant, we should escalate pricing exceptions to finance and execs.

Naomi — can you confirm whether we can share SOC 2 Type II and the data flow diagram externally under the NDA? If we need a redacted version, tell us what fields must be removed.

I've attached a quick estimate: rescope-impact-estimates.xlsx — high level revenue delta and staffing cost.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference
